subject: Reanchor plan: schedule float, MAP adjustments, and escalation path
messages:
From: Alyssa Jordan <alyssaj@healthtech.co>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft and acceptance window

Hi Chloe,

Quick note from this AM's steering: a couple of our internal teams flagged resource conflicts that will push the integration sign-off out by ~2 weeks unless we make a small schedule change on your side. We know this is tight.

Status: evaluation completed for core APIs, still running the last end-to-end test (security team runs Thursday). Procurement has a standard PO delay of 7–10 business days after contract finalization.

Question: Can we adjust the MAP to add a 10-day float and a contingency cutover window, and record that in the mutual action plan? We want one clean mutual dates table (dev -> security -> procurement -> go-live) so execs can sign off.

If you can share a versioned MAP with dates and a risk column we can circulate to stakeholders today, that would help.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Jordan
Director, Product Integrations
HealthTech Solutions

--
Attachments: none
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Jordan <alyssaj@healthtech.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Procurement <procurement@healthtech.co>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft and acceptance window

Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. I updated the MAP to reflect a 10-day schedule float and added a short "slippage mitigation" column with two fallback options: (A) staggered acceptance (core + non-critical systems) and (B) canary service rollout with reduced throughput. See attached MAP_v2_HealthTech.xlsx for the proposed dates and responsibilities.

Key asks from our side:
- Please confirm whether procurement can accept the 10-day float (we'll mark the MPA to show the acceptance window + PO target date).
- If security cannot complete the E2E by Friday, we will automatically pivot to the canary cutoff (option B).

I've also spun up a short risk log (attached) and tagged potential credit/rollback triggers so Marissa can review for a one-time concession if the schedule materially moves again. Jonas, can you take point on the risk log and add any support runbooks or additional canary acceptance criteria?

Next steps: I'll circulate the versioned MAP to your execs after procurement confirms the PO target date. If procurement needs an explicit DocuSign stagger (signature dates), please add that link and I'll route the legal redline.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v2_HealthTech.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), procurement-checklist_HealthTech.csv (attachment stub)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Alyssa Jordan <alyssaj@healthtech.co>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft and acceptance window

Chloe — I reviewed the MAP_v2 and the proposed mitigation column. We can authorize a one-time credit if HealthTech confirms the revised timeline within 48 hours and commits to the updated procurement cadence. I'll coordinate with finance for a conditional credit (terms in a short memo).

Marissa

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP draft and acceptance window — risk log and canary plan

Team — uploaded an initial slippage-risk-log and a short canary acceptance checklist. Main items I captured:
- Risk R1: Security E2E delay -> Impact: acceptance window +3 to +14 days. Mitigation: run partial end-to-end smoke by Thu PM; if fail, activate canary (limit traffic to 5% for 72 hours).
- Risk R2: PO processing -> Impact: contract effective date shift. Mitigation: procurement checklist attached; ask Alyssa to request expedited PO routing with vendor code "VT-88".
- Risk R3: Integration bug found post-acceptance -> Impact: rollback and credit eligibility. Mitigation: maintain a two-week warm support window; define rollback triggers in the MAP.

Attachments: slippage-risk-log-20270429.pdf (risk log stub)

Alyssa — I added two acceptance gates in the MAP: Gate 1 (core APIs), Gate 2 (full integration). If Gate 1 passes but Gate 2 slips we still allow a limited go-live under the canary.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 01:10:00 +0000
Subject: Final: MAP v2 accepted (conditional) — next steps and escalation path

Alyssa — thanks for the quick coordination. Per attachments and the risk log, here is the consolidated path forward: 

1) MAP v2 attached is our single source of truth. It includes the 10-day float, two acceptance gates, rollback criteria, and trigger conditions for the one-time credit (Finance to issue conditional memo).
2) Procurement: please confirm PO routing ETA by EOD Monday so we can set the contract effective date. If procurement requires DocuSign staggered signatures, use the link in my prior email and tag the signature dates in the MAP.
3) Canary fallback: if security misses the E2E window, we will run Gate 1 canary at 5% traffic for 72 hours. Jonas will own the canary runbook and the success metrics.
4) Escalation: if we see a second slip beyond the 10-day float, Marissa will escalate for exec review and decide on credits/contract amendments.

Alyssa, please reply-all to confirm procurement ETA and sign-off on the conditional acceptance. Once you confirm I'll issue the final MAP_v2 to your execs and attach the Finance memo.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAP_v2_HealthTech.xlsx, slippage-risk-log-20270429.pdf, procurement-checklist_HealthTech.csv
